name: Akris
band_note: mean of blouse and sweater entry $645 (women's price pass, 2026-10-13)
why: Women's tailoring, double-face cashmere coats, knitwear and dresses from a Swiss house, plus horsehair Ai bags at $2,090–3,190, sold through its own boutiques, site and department stores.
origin: Founded in St. Gallen, Switzerland in 1922 by Alice Kriemler-Schoch.

craft_evidence.mills: none on product pages; the horsehair page names the fibre's origin (Mongolia) but no mill; 'St. Gallen cotton and embroidery' is historical
craft_evidence.madein: 0 of 80 sampled product pages state a country
craft_evidence.heritage: dated and placed — 1922, St. Gallen, Alice Kriemler; named Akris in 1944 (/pages/our-story)
craft_evidence.process: partial — fabric pages (double-face, horsehair, cashmere) exist; double-face and cashmere render client-side and returned no text; horsehair gives provenance of the fibre, not the making
craft_evidence.reasoning: Akris's heritage is dated and placed (St. Gallen, 1922) and its site talks about ateliers in the past tense, but nothing read today says where the range is made: no country, maker or mill on 80 sampled product pages and no production site on the company page. Reputation would put it higher; the evidence on the page supports a 2 until the double-face and cashmere pages are read rendered.
